Target sources: Indeed API, LinkedIn Jobs (via RSS/scrape), USAJobs API (federal cyber jobs), CyberSecJobs, SimplyHired, ZipRecruiter. Focus filters: entry-level, junior, associate, 0-2 years experience, internships. Keywords: SOC analyst, help desk, security analyst, junior pentester, IT support, cloud associate, GRC analyst. Store results in JSON or Firestore. Run on schedule (daily or on-demand). Respect robots.txt and rate limits. Consider Cloud Functions or a lightweight Node.js cron.

sprints.title: Job Search — Build job listings browser UI with filters
sprints.notes: Frontend page that displays scraped job listings in a searchable, filterable interface. Filters: role type (SOC, help desk, pentester, cloud, GRC), location (remote, state, city), experience level, salary range, date posted, clearance required. Card layout per listing showing: title, company, location, salary range, posted date, source link, matched keywords. Sort by date, relevance, salary. Paginated or infinite scroll. Dark themed to match Prime.

sprints.title: Job Search — Map certifications to job requirements
sprints.notes: Parse job listings for certification requirements (Security+, CySA+, A+, Network+, CCNA, AWS CCP, Azure AZ-900, CEH, CISSP, etc.) and tag each listing accordingly. Cross-reference with the student's completed coursework in Prime — show a match percentage or 'You qualify' badge on listings where the student has the certs mentioned. This directly connects Prime learning to job readiness. Display cert match data on each job card.

sprints.title: Job Search — Career path explorer linking houses to roles
sprints.notes: Interactive visualization showing how each Hexworth house maps to real career paths. House of the Shield → GRC Analyst, Security Engineer, IR Lead. House of the Dark Arts → Pentester, Red Team, Bug Bounty. House of the Cloud → Cloud Security Engineer, DevSecOps. House of the Eye → SOC Analyst, Threat Hunter, SIEM Engineer. Show typical progression: entry-level → mid → senior → leadership. Include average salary ranges per role (source: BLS, CyberSeek, Glassdoor). Link to relevant job listings from JS-3.

sprints.title: Job Search — Resume and cover letter builder for cyber roles
sprints.notes: Guided resume builder tailored to entry-level cybersecurity and IT roles. Pre-populated sections: completed Hexworth coursework/certs, skills from house modules, lab experience. Templates for: SOC Analyst resume, Help Desk resume, Cloud Associate resume, Junior Pentester resume. ATS-friendly formatting (clean, parseable). Optional cover letter generator with fill-in-the-blank templates customized per role type. Export to PDF. Store drafts in localStorage or Firestore.

sprints.title: Job Search — Interview prep question bank by role
sprints.notes: Curated question bank organized by role: SOC Analyst, Help Desk, Security Analyst, Cloud Engineer, GRC, Pentester. Categories: technical (networking, OS, security concepts), behavioral (STAR format), scenario-based (what would you do if...). Pull from real interview experiences. Flashcard-style practice mode with reveal answers. Track which questions the student has practiced. Cross-reference questions to relevant Prime modules so students can review weak areas.

sprints.title: Job Search — Job alerts and saved searches
sprints.notes: Let students save search filters (e.g. 'remote SOC analyst entry-level') and get notified when new matching listings appear. Store saved searches in Firestore per user. On each scraper run, compare new listings against saved searches and flag matches. Notification options: in-app badge on Career Launchpad, email digest (requires email integration). Also allow bookmarking individual listings for later review.

sprints.title: Job Search — Salary and market data dashboard
sprints.notes: Dashboard showing real-time job market insights derived from scraped data: number of open positions by role, average salary by role and region, most requested certifications, remote vs on-site ratio, top hiring companies, trending job titles. Visualize with charts (bar, line, donut). Data sourced from scraper results + CyberSeek + BLS. Updated on each scrape cycle. Helps students understand demand and set salary expectations.

sprints.title: Job Search — Internship and apprenticeship aggregator
sprints.notes: Dedicated scraper pipeline and UI section for internships and apprenticeships specifically. Sources: Handshake, WayUp, Chegg Internships, USAJobs (Pathways program), CISA cyber internships, NSA/FBI/DoD summer programs, SANS cyber academies, corporate programs (Microsoft LEAP, Google STEP, AWS re/Start). Also scrape for apprenticeship programs (DoL registered, CyberCorps SFS, NICE apprenticeships). Separate filters: paid vs unpaid, summer vs year-round, clearance-eligible, academic credit, remote-friendly. Tag with application deadlines and highlight closing-soon listings. Display as a dedicated tab or section within Career Launchpad alongside the main job board.

sprints.title: Grant Finder — Design Funding Hub page and navigation
sprints.notes: Design a new section in Prime called 'Funding Hub' or 'Grant Finder' accessible from the main dashboard. Hub page with cards linking to: grant aggregator, scholarship search, funding calendar, application tracker, proposal resources. Target audiences: (1) students seeking tuition/cert exam funding, (2) educators/institutions seeking cybersecurity program grants, (3) small businesses seeking cyber resilience funding. Dark themed to match Prime. Route: _app/funding/ or _app/grants/.

sprints.title: Grant Finder — Build federal grant scraper (grants.gov, SAM.gov)
sprints.notes: Build scraper/API integration for federal cybersecurity and IT education grants. Primary sources: Grants.gov API (search by CFDA codes for cyber/IT education), SAM.gov (contract opportunities), NSF (CyberCorps SFS, SaTC program), DHS/CISA (cyber workforce grants), DoD (CySP, SMART scholarship), DoE (Title III/V for minority-serving institutions). Filter by: eligibility (individual, institution, small business, nonprofit), funding amount, deadline, grant type (research, workforce, education, infrastructure). Store results in JSON or Firestore. Daily refresh.

sprints.title: Grant Finder — Build private/industry funding scraper
sprints.notes: Scrape and aggregate non-federal cybersecurity funding sources. Targets: (ISC)² Foundation scholarships, CompTIA scholarships, SANS CyberStart/scholarships, EC-Council scholarships, WiCyS scholarships, ISACA Foundation, CyberCorps SFS, Raytheon/RTX cyber scholarships, Google cybersecurity certificate funding, AWS re/Start program, Microsoft TEALS, Cisco Networking Academy grants, ISSA Education Foundation, CrowdStrike Foundation, Palo Alto Cybersecurity Academy. Also: state-level workforce development grants (WIOA funds for cyber training). Categorize by: student scholarships, institutional program grants, workforce development, small business cyber grants (SBA, SBIR/STTR for cyber startups).

sprints.title: Grant Finder — Build grant listings browser UI with filters
sprints.notes: Frontend page displaying all aggregated grants/scholarships in a searchable, filterable interface. Filters: funding type (scholarship, grant, contract, fellowship), eligibility (student, educator, institution, small business, veteran, minority-serving, women in cyber), amount range, deadline status (open, closing soon, upcoming), source (federal, private, corporate, state), focus area (education, workforce, research, infrastructure, small business resilience). Card layout per listing: title, funder, amount, deadline, eligibility summary, direct link. Sort by deadline, amount, relevance. Highlight closing-soon with urgency badges.

sprints.title: Grant Finder — Funding deadline calendar with alerts
sprints.notes: Visual calendar view showing grant/scholarship deadlines plotted by month. Color-coded by type: blue for federal, orange for corporate, green for scholarships, purple for state/local. Click a date to see all grants due. Export to iCal/Google Calendar. Allow students to subscribe to specific grants and receive in-app reminders at 30-day, 7-day, and 1-day marks before deadline. Recurring grants (annual programs) auto-populate for next cycle based on historical dates.

sprints.title: Grant Finder — Application tracker and status board
sprints.notes: Personal Kanban-style board for tracking grant/scholarship applications. Columns: Researching → Preparing → Submitted → Under Review → Awarded/Denied. Each card shows: grant name, funder, amount, deadline, required documents checklist, submission date, status notes. Drag-and-drop between columns. Store in Firestore per user. Dashboard summary: total applied, total awarded, pending amount, success rate. Helps students stay organized across multiple applications.

sprints.title: Grant Finder — Proposal writing resources and templates
sprints.notes: Resource library for writing competitive grant proposals and scholarship applications. Include: grant writing guide (abstract, narrative, budget, evaluation plan), scholarship essay templates and examples, personal statement framework for cyber careers, budget template for institutional grants, letters of support templates, common mistakes to avoid. Organized by grant type: student scholarship essay vs institutional program proposal vs small business SBIR. Presentation-style pages matching Prime's dark theme.

sprints.title: Grant Finder — Eligibility matcher based on student profile
sprints.notes: Let students fill out a profile (or auto-populate from Prime data): enrolled institution type (community college, HBCU, HSI, tribal college, 4-year university), veteran status, demographics, GPA range, field of study, certifications earned, state of residence, US citizen/permanent resident. Run profile against all grants to show a personalized 'You May Qualify' feed ranked by match strength. Highlight grants specifically targeting the student's demographics or institution type. Update recommendations as new grants are scraped.

sprints.title: Grant Finder — Small business cyber grant section
sprints.notes: Dedicated section for small business cybersecurity funding. Sources: SBA cybersecurity resources, SBIR/STTR grants for cyber startups, state small business cyber resilience grants, NIST MEP cybersecurity assistance, FCC Cybersecurity Pilot Program, CISA cyber resilience grants for critical infrastructure small businesses. Also include: cyber insurance guidance, free security assessment programs (CISA cyber hygiene services), and low-cost compliance tools. This extends the Funding Hub beyond education into the broader industry ecosystem.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Design hub page and cross-house navigation
sprints.notes: Design 'The Hunting Grounds' — the bug hunting hub page. This is a cross-house area accessible from multiple houses (dark-arts, web, code, cloud, shield, key, script, eye). Landing page should feature: hero section with hunting motif, skill-path selector (web, mobile, API, cloud, network, crypto), difficulty tiers (Beginner Tracker → Intermediate Hunter → Elite Stalker), leaderboard preview, and quick-start guide. Navigation should allow entry from any relevant house page. Register in content-registry.js as a multi-house content area. Use warm dark theme with accent colors that blend across houses — consider a unique 'hunting' accent (forest green or blood red) that distinguishes it from any single house.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Bug bounty platform guide and onboarding
sprints.notes: Comprehensive guide to bug bounty platforms and getting started. Cover: HackerOne (largest program list, beginner-friendly), Bugcrowd (curated programs, VRT vulnerability taxonomy), Intigriti (EU-focused, ethical emphasis), Synack (invite-only, Red Team model), YesWeHack (European leader), Open Bug Bounty (responsible disclosure, no exploit required). For each platform: how to sign up, profile optimization, reputation systems, payout structures, program selection strategy. Include: how to read program scopes and rules of engagement, legal considerations (CFAA, international law), setting up a dedicated hunting environment (VM, VPN, note-taking), and a 'First Bug in 30 Days' roadmap for beginners.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Reconnaissance and asset discovery methodology
sprints.notes: Deep-dive into recon methodology — the foundation of bug hunting. Passive recon: OSINT techniques, Shodan/Censys/ZoomEye, certificate transparency logs (crt.sh), DNS enumeration (subfinder, amass, assetfinder), Google dorking, Wayback Machine mining, GitHub/GitLab secret scanning, social media OSINT, WHOIS analysis. Active recon: port scanning (nmap, masscan, rustscan), directory brute-forcing (ffuf, dirsearch, gobuster), technology fingerprinting (Wappalyzer, WhatWeb, httpx), virtual host discovery, parameter discovery (Arjun, ParamSpider), JavaScript file analysis (LinkFinder, JSFinder), API endpoint enumeration. Include: recon automation workflows (bash scripting, recon pipelines), organizing findings with tools like Notion/Obsidian/BurpSuite, and a recon checklist template. Cross-references script house for automation content.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Web application vulnerability hunting guides
sprints.notes: Comprehensive web app bug hunting guides organized by vulnerability class. Each guide covers: what it is, why it matters, how to find it, proof-of-concept creation, impact demonstration, and remediation. Vulnerability classes: XSS (reflected, stored, DOM-based, mutation XSS, blind XSS via XSSHunter), SQL Injection (union-based, blind boolean, time-based, second-order, NoSQL injection), SSRF (basic, blind, partial, cloud metadata pivoting to AWS/GCP/Azure IMDS), IDOR (direct reference, indirect reference, parameter tampering, UUID prediction), CSRF (token bypass, login CSRF, JSON CSRF), Authentication bugs (2FA bypass, password reset poisoning, OAuth misconfigs, JWT attacks), Authorization flaws (privilege escalation, horizontal/vertical, role manipulation), Business logic bugs (race conditions, price manipulation, coupon abuse, workflow bypass), File upload vulnerabilities (extension bypass, content-type tricks, polyglot files), Open redirect chains, CORS misconfigurations, subdomain takeover, HTTP request smuggling, cache poisoning, prototype pollution. Each guide should include real-world disclosed examples (redacted) and practice scenarios.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — API security testing methodology
sprints.notes: Dedicated API bug hunting guide. REST API testing: endpoint discovery, authentication testing (API keys, OAuth tokens, JWT), broken object-level authorization (BOLA/IDOR), broken function-level authorization, mass assignment, rate limiting bypass, injection via API parameters, verbose error messages, improper asset management (zombie/shadow APIs). GraphQL testing: introspection queries, batching attacks, nested query DoS, authorization bypass via field-level access, mutation abuse. gRPC testing: reflection abuse, message tampering. API documentation analysis: Swagger/OpenAPI spec mining, Postman collection extraction, undocumented endpoint discovery. Tools: Burp Suite with API-specific extensions, Postman, Insomnia, mitmproxy, OWASP ZAP API scan, kiterunner for API endpoint brute-forcing. Include OWASP API Security Top 10 mapped to hunting techniques.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Cloud misconfiguration hunting
sprints.notes: Cloud-specific bug hunting methodology. AWS: open S3 buckets (lazy S3, bucket-finder), exposed EC2 metadata (IMDS v1 vs v2), overpermissive IAM policies, public RDS/ElasticSearch/Lambda, CloudFront misconfigs, SQS/SNS exposure, Cognito pool enumeration. Azure: blob storage enumeration, Azure AD tenant discovery, exposed App Services, Key Vault access misconfigs, Azure Functions auth bypass. GCP: public Cloud Storage buckets, Firebase database exposure (common in mobile apps), GCP metadata server, Cloud Functions auth issues. Multi-cloud: Kubernetes misconfigs (exposed dashboards, etcd, kubelet), Docker registry exposure, Terraform state file leaks, CI/CD pipeline secrets. Tools: ScoutSuite, Prowler, CloudMapper, Pacu, enumerate-iam, cloud_enum. Include: how to identify cloud infrastructure from external recon (IP ranges, SSL certs, HTTP headers), responsible cloud disclosure processes.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Mobile application bug hunting
sprints.notes: Mobile app bug hunting guides for Android and iOS. Android: APK reverse engineering (jadx, apktool, dex2jar), dynamic analysis with Frida, intercepting traffic with Burp/mitmproxy (certificate pinning bypass), insecure data storage (SharedPreferences, SQLite, logs), hardcoded secrets and API keys, exported activities/services/broadcast receivers, deep link abuse, WebView vulnerabilities, intent injection. iOS: IPA analysis (class-dump, Hopper, otool), runtime manipulation with Frida/objection, Keychain data extraction, plist inspection, URL scheme hijacking, universal link validation bypass, App Transport Security bypass. Cross-platform: Firebase database enumeration (common goldmine), API endpoint extraction from binaries, push notification abuse, OAuth/SSO implementation flaws in mobile. Tools: MobSF (automated scanner), Objection, Drozer, Genymotion. Include setup guides for mobile testing lab (rooted Android, jailbroken iOS simulator).

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Network and infrastructure vulnerability hunting
sprints.notes: Network-layer and infrastructure bug hunting. Port/service enumeration: nmap scripting engine (NSE), service version detection, default credential testing (Hydra, Medusa), SNMP enumeration, SMB/NFS share discovery. Protocol-level: DNS zone transfer, DNS rebinding, BGP hijacking concepts, SSL/TLS misconfigs (testssl.sh, sslyze — expired certs, weak ciphers, HSTS absence), mail server misconfigs (open relays, SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures, email spoofing). Infrastructure: VPN misconfigs, exposed admin panels (Shodan queries), printer/IoT device exposure, IPMI/BMC access, exposed database ports (MongoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch, Memcached). Wireless: rogue AP detection, WPA2 enterprise misconfigs. Include: how network bugs fit into bug bounty scope (many programs include infrastructure), mapping external attack surface, and integration with shield house defensive perspective.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Cryptographic vulnerability hunting
sprints.notes: Crypto-focused bug hunting techniques. JWT attacks: algorithm confusion (none, HS256 vs RS256), weak signing secrets (jwt_tool, hashcat), JWK injection, kid parameter injection, claim manipulation. Session management: predictable session tokens, session fixation, cookie security flags (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite). Encryption flaws: padding oracle attacks, ECB mode detection (penguin problem), weak key generation, hardcoded encryption keys, IV reuse. Certificate issues: self-signed certs in production, expired certificates, wildcard cert abuse, certificate transparency monitoring. Password storage: identifying weak hashing (MD5, SHA1 without salt), timing attacks on comparisons. Randomness: weak PRNG detection, predictable tokens/codes (password reset, email verification, API keys). Cross-references key house cryptography curriculum for foundational knowledge.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Source code review and static analysis
sprints.notes: Source code review techniques for vulnerability discovery. White-box hunting: reading source for sinks (dangerous functions), tracing data flow from sources to sinks, identifying authentication/authorization gaps, spotting race conditions, finding hardcoded secrets. Language-specific patterns: JavaScript (eval, innerHTML, postMessage, prototype pollution), Python (pickle deserialization, format string injection, SSTI via Jinja2/Mako), PHP (unserialize, include, preg_replace /e), Java (deserialization gadgets, JNDI injection, XXE), Ruby (ERB injection, mass assignment, send/public_send). SAST tools: Semgrep (custom rules), CodeQL (GitHub), SonarQube, Bandit (Python), Brakeman (Ruby), SpotBugs (Java), ESLint security plugins. Open-source audit: finding bugs in OSS dependencies (npm audit, Snyk, dependency confusion), reviewing recent commits for security-relevant changes, GitHub Advanced Security features. Include: how to set up a code review workflow, triaging findings, and writing reports from code review discoveries.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Tool arsenal guides and lab setup
sprints.notes: Comprehensive tool guides and hunting environment setup. Core tools: Burp Suite (Community vs Pro — interceptor, repeater, intruder, scanner, extensions like Autorize, Logger++, Param Miner, ActiveScan++), OWASP ZAP (scripting, fuzzing, API scanning), browser dev tools for manual testing. Recon tools: Amass, subfinder, httpx, nuclei, katana, gau, waybackurls. Fuzzing: ffuf, wfuzz, Turbo Intruder. Exploitation: sqlmap, XSStrike, tplmap, SSRFmap, Commix. Automation: Nuclei template writing (custom checks), bash/Python scripting for recon pipelines, GitHub Actions for continuous recon. Environment setup: Kali Linux / ParrotOS configuration, VPN for bug hunting, virtual machine lab, Burp CA certificate installation, browser profile for hunting (extensions: FoxyProxy, Wappalyzer, Cookie-Editor, HackBar). Include a 'starter kit' checklist for new hunters — minimal tools to install on day one.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Practice targets and vulnerable lab directory
sprints.notes: Curated directory of practice targets for skill building. Intentionally vulnerable apps: DVWA, bWAPP, WebGoat, Juice Shop, HackTheBox, TryHackMe, PortSwigger Web Security Academy (free, gold standard for web), PentesterLab, VulnHub, Damn Vulnerable GraphQL, OWASP Mutillidae, NodeGoat, RailsGoat, CloudGoat (AWS), flAWS.cloud, Thunder CTF (GCP), AzureGoat. Bug bounty training: Hacker101 CTF (HackerOne), Bugcrowd University, Nahamsec's resources, InsiderPhD YouTube series, STÖK hunting methodology. Organize by: skill level (beginner/intermediate/advanced), vulnerability type, technology stack. Track completion progress through Prime's ProgressSystem. Link to relevant BH guides for each target type. Include a 'graduation path' — when you can find X consistently in labs, you're ready for real programs.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Report writing and disclosure templates
sprints.notes: Bug report writing mastery — the difference between a duplicate/informative and a bounty. Report structure: title (clear, specific), vulnerability type, severity assessment (CVSS calculator walkthrough), affected endpoint/parameter, steps to reproduce (numbered, exact), proof of concept (screenshots, video, curl commands), impact statement (what can an attacker actually do?), remediation recommendations. Templates for common vuln types: XSS report, IDOR report, SSRF report, auth bypass report, business logic report. Common mistakes that get reports closed: insufficient PoC, self-XSS, theoretical impact without demonstration, duplicate hunting (how to search for prior reports), out-of-scope submissions. Advanced: chaining low-severity bugs into high-impact chains, writing for maximum impact assessment, communicating with triage teams, handling disputes. Include downloadable Markdown report templates.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Vulnerability taxonomy and classification reference
sprints.notes: Interactive reference for vulnerability classification systems. OWASP Top 10 (Web, API, Mobile, LLM) — each entry with hunting-specific guidance, not just definitions. CWE (Common Weakness Enumeration) — searchable/filterable database of relevant CWEs mapped to bug bounty categories. CVSS v3.1/v4.0 calculator — interactive tool to score findings with explanation of each metric (Attack Vector, Attack Complexity, Privileges Required, User Interaction, Scope, CIA impact). Bugcrowd VRT (Vulnerability Rating Taxonomy) — practical severity guide that maps to bounty payouts. MITRE ATT&CK mapping for relevant techniques. Cross-reference: for each vulnerability class, link to the relevant BH hunting guide, practice targets, and report templates. Build as an interactive searchable/filterable applet using Prime's existing applet infrastructure.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Responsible disclosure and ethics guide
sprints.notes: Legal and ethical framework for bug hunting. Legal landscape: CFAA (US), Computer Misuse Act (UK), EU Directive on attacks against information systems, safe harbor provisions, DOJ policy on good-faith security research (2022 update). Responsible disclosure: coordinated disclosure vs full disclosure, disclosure timelines (90-day standard), handling unresponsive vendors, when to involve CERT/CC, disclosure through platforms vs direct vendor contact. Ethics: staying in scope, not accessing/exfiltrating user data, not disrupting services, not using automated tools aggressively (rate limiting your own scans), reporting vs exploiting, chain escalation ethics (when to stop chaining). Case studies: notable disclosure successes and failures, researchers who got in trouble and why, companies with exemplary response programs. Include: a personal code of conduct template, and how Hexworth students should approach responsible hunting.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Bug bounty portfolio and achievement tracker
sprints.notes: Personal dashboard for tracking bug hunting progress and building a portfolio. Features: log submitted reports (platform, program, vuln type, severity, status, payout), track acceptance rate, visualize findings by category (pie/bar charts), earnings tracker with monthly/yearly summaries, skill heatmap showing strong/weak areas, streak tracking (days active), personal best records. Portfolio builder: generate a shareable (anonymized) portfolio page showing stats, top findings (redacted), platforms active on, reputation scores, specializations. Integration with Prime's ProgressSystem and LeaderboardManager for cross-platform gamification. Achievement badges: First Blood (first accepted bug), Chain Master (first bug chain), Five-Figure (cumulative $10k+), Specialist (10+ of same vuln type), Polyglot (bugs across 5+ platforms). Useful for job applications — demonstrates practical security skills.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Automation and continuous recon pipelines
sprints.notes: Build automation workflows for efficient bug hunting. Continuous recon: set up scheduled subdomain monitoring (new subdomains = fresh attack surface), automated port scanning on new assets, screenshot capture pipelines (Aquatone, Gowitness, EyeWitness), content change detection (monitoring for new endpoints, JS files, API versions). Notification pipelines: Slack/Discord/email alerts for new assets, nuclei scan results pushed to webhook, monitor certificate transparency logs for target domains. Nuclei template development: writing custom templates for organization-specific checks, template sharing and community templates, chaining templates for complex detection logic. Pipeline architectures: simple bash scripts → Python frameworks → cloud-based recon (Axiom, ReconFTW, LazyRecon, AutoRecon). Include: cost-effective cloud recon setup (cheap VPS, free tier abuse for ethical scanning), managing scan data with ProjectDiscovery's toolchain. Cross-references script house automation content.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Writeup library and case study collection
sprints.notes: Curated collection of bug bounty writeups and case studies for learning. Categories: by vulnerability type (XSS writeups, SSRF writeups, etc.), by platform (HackerOne disclosed reports, Bugcrowd public disclosures), by target industry (fintech, social media, e-commerce, government), by bounty amount (low-hanging fruit vs high-value chains). For each writeup: summary of the finding, recon steps that led to discovery, exploitation chain, report excerpt, lessons learned, what to look for in similar targets. Featured series: 'How I Found My First Bug' stories from diverse hunters, '$10K+ Bug Stories' deep dives, 'Bug Chains That Changed the Game' (complex multi-step exploits). Include community contribution pathway — students can submit their own anonymized writeups. Regularly updated with fresh public disclosures. Organized as a searchable, tagged library using existing content infrastructure.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Hunting challenges and CTF integration
sprints.notes: Interactive bug hunting challenges built into the platform. Beginner challenges: pre-configured vulnerable apps with guided walkthroughs, hint system, step-by-step solutions. Intermediate challenges: realistic scenarios with multiple vulnerability classes, minimal hints, time-based scoring. Advanced challenges: black-box targets, chaining required, minimal context (simulates real bug bounty). Challenge categories mapped to BH guides: XSS challenges, IDOR challenges, SSRF challenges, API challenges, cloud challenges, crypto challenges. Integration with dark-arts CTF leaderboard — hunting challenges earn CTF points. Weekly/monthly rotating challenges to keep content fresh. Use Prime's existing hive/engine challenge infrastructure where applicable. Leverage workshop/ for hosting vulnerable applications. Include: challenge creation guide for instructors to add their own scenarios.

sprints.title: The Hunting Grounds — Cross-house integration and learning paths
sprints.notes: Wire The Hunting Grounds into the broader Hexworth ecosystem.
